Nuevo León Governor Samuel García has announced a proposed $200 million expansion of the Colombia–Laredo International Bridge — a plan that would add two entirely new bridges, one for exports and one for imports, and double the crossing's lane capacity from 8 to 16.

According to Texas Border Business, the project was presented during García's visit to Texas on August 28, 2026, and construction is expected to begin in May 2027 — if the approvals and financing fall into place.

The plan calls for each of the two new bridges to have four lanes, according to a 2025 announcement by Nuevo León officials. The goal: cut truck wait times and move more freight between Mexico and Texas. García said the state's objective is roughly 15,000 daily crossings at the Colombia crossing by 2030 — up from about 7,000 daily truck crossings in 2026, and a staggering jump from roughly 300 a day in 2021.

The price tag, García said, would be split evenly: $100 million from Texas, $100 million from Nuevo León. But here is the catch citizens should note — the announcement did not say Texas authorities have given final approval for that funding. A $200 million bridge that Texas has not yet signed off on paying for is a proposal, not a promise.

The proposal has been working its way through the process for years. According to the Nuevo León government, García asked the City of Laredo for authorization in August 2023, and the Laredo City Council approved the request unanimously. In April 2025, the U.S. Department of State authorized the proposed expansion and sent its determination to the White House for a presidential permit — described at the time as the remaining U.S. authorization required.

García framed the crossing as central to Nuevo León's economic strategy: "For Nuevo León, it is essential to have the infrastructure ready to be part of this triangle," he said, referring to commercial connections with Dallas, Houston, Brownsville, Corpus Christi, Austin, San Antonio and Laredo.

The expansion is part of a wider infrastructure package: improvements to State Highway 001 North linking the Salinas Victoria industrial area with Anáhuac and the Colombia crossing, the recently completed concrete rehabilitation of the existing bridge, the expansion of the Ribereña Highway from two to four lanes, and a proposed industrial development zone in Anáhuac with tax incentives under Mexico's Plan México initiative.

Watch this one closely: the May 2027 construction date and the financing both remain subject to approvals that have not yet been locked down. Webb Watch will follow whether Texas actually commits its $100 million share — because without it, there is no bridge.

Sources: Texas Border Business, "Nuevo León Announces $200 Million Expansion of Colombia–Laredo International Bridge" (October 23, 2026) — https://texasborderbusiness.com/nuevo-leon-announces-200-million-expansion-of-colombia-laredo-international-bridge/

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Nuevo León proposes a $200 million expansion of the Colombia–Laredo bridge — two new bridges, 8 to 16 lanes — but Texas hasn't confirmed its $100 million share yet.
title: $200 Million Bridge Plan: Colombia–Laredo Crossing Would Double Capacity — If Texas Pays
